title: Bulk label printing
problem: Shipping clerks at mid-size warehouses print carrier labels one order at a time. At peak a clerk spends 11 minutes per wave of 50 orders clicking through order pages, and label printing drives 140 support tickets a month (18% of all tickets). Two enterprise prospects listed batch printing as a blocker in Q-review notes.
users:
- Shipping clerk at a 20-200 order/hour warehouse
- Warehouse supervisor who plans pick waves
goals:
- Median time to print a 50-order wave: 11 min -> under 2 min
- Label-printing support tickets: 140/month -> under 40/month within 60 days of GA
- 60% of active warehouses use bulk print weekly by day 90
non_goals:
- Rate shopping across carriers
- Printing packing slips or invoices
- Thermal printer driver management
requirements:
- Select up to 200 orders from the order list and print all labels as one PDF
- Show which orders failed and why

- P0: Select up to 200 orders from the order list and print all labels as one PDF in under 30 seconds
- P0: Show which orders failed (address invalid, carrier error) and let the clerk retry just those
- P1: Save a selection as a wave and reprint it
- P2: Sort labels to match the pick path
risks:
- Carrier API rate limits at 200 labels per batch are unknown
- Merging 200 PDFs may exceed browser memory on older warehouse PCs
- Open question: do we charge for this on the Starter plan?
launch: Feature flag for 10 design-partner warehouses for two weeks, then 25% of Growth plans, then GA if ticket volume and error rate hold
